items.mnemonic_text: An outer frame, and set inside it another box with a bar ruled across — a mask hung on a wall, with the flat plane of the cheeks around it and the eyes cut into the middle. It shows you nothing of whoever is behind it. All you get is the front of the thing, its <radical>face</radical>.

A hand has got hold of a loose flap at the top left, and you can see its fingers braced at the bottom right as it drags downward in one long, steady pull. What comes away in that pull, in a single unbroken sheet with nothing torn, is the hide: the <radical>skin</radical> taken off whole.

A net stretched flat across the top, and underneath it a shell — the old money, before coins. You spread the net, you sweep the shells in, and you hand them over the counter for whatever was on the shelf. Shells going out under a net is what it looks like to <radical>buy</radical> something.

Two uprights with a bar across them and one short stroke floating in the middle of the gap. That stroke is a mouthful being held on the tongue, right between the teeth, and nobody is in a hurry to swallow it. You only hold food in your mouth like that when it is <radical>sweet</radical>.

A figure drawn side-on: a head at the top, then a torso thickened out through the middle, and one stroke swinging down and away underneath for the legs. It is a person seen as a shape rather than a face — height, weight, the way they carry themselves. The whole physical <radical>body</radical>.

A lid across the top, then a wide vessel with a bar ruled across its middle and legs under it. It is a narrow-necked jar standing on the floor, sealed, with the line showing how far down the liquid has got. Nobody seals a jar like that for water. It is a <radical>sake jar</radical>.

A shallow container drawn face-on: two walls, a flat base, and a pair of uprights inside marking the ridges. It is far too shallow to be a pot and far too wide to be a cup. Set it down on the table and put the food on it, because it is a <radical>dish</radical>.

Three strokes crowded down the left edge: a short flick at the top, then a long stroke dropping and curving, then a leg kicking out. It is a beast in profile, all snout and haunch, pressed up against the side of the character and ready to bolt. Whenever this is on the left, the word is about an <radical>animal</radical>.
